strategy.summary: Reproduce the complex-input dtype bug in numpy.linalg.cond by building numpy at the buggy commit b7e5173c13d1 and running the PR's new TestCond tests. The decisive failures are the dtype assertions in test_cond_dtypes for complex dtypes with p in {1,-1,'fro',inf,-inf}, which return complex instead of real on the buggy revision and pass once _realType is applied in the fix.

system_packages: a C/C++ and Fortran-capable compiler toolchain (gcc or clang with gfortran or equivalent)
a BLAS/LAPACK provider (OpenBLAS or the bundled default)
pinned_because: Python 3.7.7 is only the issue-reporter environment (issue#18304) and is not a documented constraint; the buggy commit's build system is modern (meson), so 3.12 is chosen by this plan, not by evidence
numpy is unbounded in the context; it is built from source at the buggy commit so the code under test is the buggy code, not a released wheel
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md with no version constraint; latest compatible versions are chosen

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/linalg/tests/test_linalg.py::TestCond::test_cond_dtypes (parametrized over dtype in [single, double, csingle, cdouble] and norm_ord in [1, -1, 2, -2, 'fro', inf, -inf]); test_basic_nonsvd is also parametrized with is_complex but is not the decisive failure
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision b7e5173c13d1, test_cond_dtypes fails for the csingle and cdouble cases with norm_ord in {1,-1,'fro',inf,-inf}, each raising an AssertionError from assert_equal because linalg.cond(...).dtype is complex64/complex128 where float32/float64 is expected; the real-dtype cases and the 2/-2 cases still pass. On the fixed revision (buggy plus PR #29500, which adds result_t = _realType(result_t) in cond), all TestCond tests pass, including every test_cond_dtypes case.
strategy.numerical_probe: linalg.cond(A.astype(complex128), p=1).dtype versus linalg.cond(A.astype(complex128), p=2).dtype on the 3x3 matrix [[1,0,1],[0,-2,0],[0,0,3]]; the dtype comparison is the signal, not the printed value

input_output_examples.expected_output: 253.11513101087314 as a real float64 (no complex dtype)
126.26418916571008 as a real float64 (no complex dtype)

risks: The issue's example uses unseeded random matrices, so printed values are not reproducible; only the dtype pattern is stable and is what the test checks

Test assertions depend on get_real_dtype being importable in test_linalg.py at the buggy revision; the PR diff does not show an import change, so if it is missing the test errors on both revisions and does not transition

The given test_commands entry uses numpy.test(), which is not the project's pytest path and may be removed or behave differently across numpy versions; this plan runs pytest directly on the test file instead
Building numpy at this commit requires a working meson/ninja toolchain and BLAS/LAPACK; if the build fails the transition cannot be observed
Running pytest from the source root may import the source tree or an installed numpy; ensure the editable install is the one imported, otherwise the buggy code is not exercised

Only the dtype path is decisive; the value assertions in test_basic_nonsvd use assert_almost_equal, which compares complex 4+0j to 4 numerically, so test_basic_nonsvd[True] likely passes on the buggy revision and does not provide the transition

The bug is platform independent (no architecture, sanitiser, or threading dependence in the evidence), so no special platform is required; the era of the reporter's environment (numpy 1.19.1, Python 3.7.7) is not needed to reproduce a dtype bug that the fix addresses on main

oracle.reference_source: test_cond_dtypes compares the dtype of linalg.cond output to get_real_dtype(dtype), exact dtype equality; value checks in test_basic_nonsvd use assert_almost_equal with default decimal precision
oracle.why: The transition is decided by dtype equality, which is exact, not by a numerical tolerance

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_cond_dtypes csingle/cdouble cases for p in {1,-1,'fro',inf,-inf} hit assert_equal on .dtype and see complex64/complex128 where float32/float64 is expected, so AssertionError is raised; this is why the test fails on the buggy revision.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With result_t = _realType(result_t) in cond, linalg.cond returns real dtype for complex inputs for every p, so all test_cond_dtypes cases match get_real_dtype(dtype) and TestCond passes.
